answers.evidence:
I built a minimal Go daemon simulator (`httptest` + exact-key `map[string]json.RawMessage` PUT handler, `fleet.toml`-sourced projects surviving restart, API-only projects reverted to default 900 on restart) and ran the fix against it with `go vet` clean.

```
PASS  create api-only project via PUT
INFO  after restart, idle-worker = {"Name":"idle-worker","CooldownS":900,"Source":"api"} (expected revert to 900)
PASS  FIX: re-PUT CooldownS 43200 PascalCase after restart
INFO  after restart, persistent-job (fleet.toml) = {"Name":"persistent-job","CooldownS":43200,"Source":"fleet.toml"} (must stay 43200)
PASS  fleet.toml entry survives restart
PASS  lowercase cooldownS key is rejected (why PascalCase matters)
INFO  final idle-worker GET = {"Name":"idle-worker","CooldownS":900,"Source":"api"}
SUMMARY: 0 failures
```

**Verified behaviors / edge cases:**
- **Bug reproduced:** API-only project at 43200 reverts to 900 after simulated restart.
- **Fix works:** re-PUT with `{"CooldownS":43200}` + separate GET verify passes and detects any drift (returns error on mismatch).
- **Permanence:** `fleet.toml`-sourced project stays 43200 across restart with no PUT.
- **Case sensitivity:** lowercase `{"cooldownS":43200}` is rejected (400) — the PascalCase requirement is real, not cosmetic.
- **Volatility caveat confirmed:** an API-only project still reverts on a *later* restart even after re-PUT — hence the `fleet.toml` recommendation, and the GET verify is what catches it instead of the tick's "no drift" claim.
